summary: Gives short descriptive acronyms to the three numeric fields of the TLSA record used by DANE, because people kept getting confused when discussing them. It also updates the format of the IANA registry created by RFC 6698 to carry these names.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds descriptive names to the three numeric fields in TLSA records. The acronyms make the registry easier for people to read and do not change the DANE protocol.

subtitle: Adds descriptive acronyms for the three numeric fields in TLSA records.

tldr.problem: People were confused about the meaning and order of the three numeric TLSA fields.
tldr.mechanism: IANA adds acronym columns to the TLSA certificate-usage, selector, and matching-type sub-registries.
tldr.outcome: The change improves human-readable registry entries without changing DANE protocol behavior; it updates RFC 6698.

today: RFC 7218 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6698. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7218.

sections.title: Replacing Confusing Numbers with Names
sections.content:
People discussing DANE repeatedly confused the three numeric TLSA fields and their order. This RFC updates the IANA registry format to add an acronym for each field.

The document does not change DANE behavior. It says software that parses TLSA records is expected to accept the acronyms in upper, mixed, or lower case.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry shows short names alongside the field numbers. This helps people discuss the fields without changing how TLSA works.

sections.title: Acronyms for the Three Fields
sections.content:
The certificate-usage registry includes PKIX-TA, PKIX-EE, DANE-TA, and DANE-EE. The selector registry includes Cert and SPKI. The matching-type registry includes Full, SHA2-256, and SHA2-512.

Each registry also has a private-use value 255, named PrivCert, PrivSel, or PrivMatch as appropriate.
sections.plainLanguage: Each numeric field now has names that describe its setting. The names are for human use and are not case-sensitive.

sections.title: Examples and Security
sections.content:
The RFC shows TLSA records written with names such as PKIX-TA CERT SHA2-512 instead of the corresponding numeric values. It also shows how a protocol specification can state which named settings it accepts.

The security section says that this document changes registry fields only and does not change protocol behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: Specifications can use the acronyms to make accepted TLSA settings easier to read. The protocol itself behaves the same way.
